newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn, states agree to split East German debts.
newsitem.headline: Bonn, states agree to split East German debts.

text.p: Germany has reached a compromise on carving up and repaying billions of marks in delinquent debt piled up by municipal authorities in communist East Germany, the Social Democrat (SPD) opposition said on Wednesday.

The deal, reached in parliament's mediation process, would split 8.4 billion marks ($5.12 billion) in debt down the middle between the Bonn federal government and east German federal states, SPD parliamentary manager Peter Struck said.
Struck added that debt repayments would begin in 1998.
The compromise means that no extra burden will fall on already-strained state finances this year -- when Bonn wants to qualify for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999.
The government forecasts a budget deficit of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product -- just below the three percent limit set by the Maastricht treaty.

The agreement ends a battle lasting over a year in which Bonn, despite funnelling over 100 billion marks annually in aid to the east, demanded repayment of loans made by East Berlin for local projects like schools and sports facilities.

Eastern state governments had resisted, saying that Bonn had forgiven other debts that predated unification in 1990, and arguing that local government had little choice but to accept money for projects they had not wanted to build.

Earlier, Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl said that Bonn would take over the old debts owed by Berlin. Germany's new capital is nearly broke and last autumn imposed harsh austerity measures to shore up city finances.

But, in a deal struck between Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Berlin Mayor Eberhard Diepgen, state transfers to Berlin would be reduced as a result of Bonn picking up an annual 35 million mark bill for debt service.

Debts to be repaid by the remaining five east German states will be shared out equally. The distribution won the consent of Saxony state, which had opposed linking the debt repayment to the populations of the different provinces.

Struck said the deal, reached in parliamentary mediation -- the last resort for deadlocked measures -- should be approved on Thursday in the Bundestag lower house of parliament and in the Bundesrat upper house on Friday. ($1=1.6405 Mark)
